Circled Times Symbol

There is no legacy Windows Alt code for Circled Times because it is not in either the OEM code page 437 or Windows-1252 tables. The Unicode codepoint is U+2297, which you can use as ⊗ in HTML, \2297 in CSS, or type with Alt+8855 on Windows (BMP only). If your keyboard has no numeric keypad, use the Character Viewer, the HTML entity, or copy the character directly. Circled Times is outside both legacy code pages, which is why U+2297 is the identifier that works across Word, HTML, CSS, Python and JavaScript. HTML also defines the named entity ⊗ for Circled Times, but the numeric form ⊗ is safer when compatibility is uncertain.

How to type circled times on Windows

  1. Turn Num Lock on so the numeric keypad is active.
  2. Hold the left Alt key.
  3. Type 8 8 5 5 on the numeric keypad for the decimal codepoint 8855.
  4. Release Alt. The Circled Times character (⊗) appears.

If your keyboard has no numeric keypad, see how to type symbols without a numpad.

How to type circled times on macOS

There is no direct Option shortcut for Circled Times. Open the Character Viewer with ⌃⌘Space, search for "Circled Times" and click the character to insert it.

How to use circled times in code

  • HTML: or , also
  • CSS: content:"\2297"; ()
  • Python: \u2297 or chr(0x2297)
  • JavaScript: \u2297 or String.fromCodePoint(0x2297)
  • JSON: "\u2297"
  • LaTeX: $\otimes$ (math mode)

Frequently asked questions

Is there an Alt code for ⊗?

No legacy Alt code exists for Circled Times because it is not in code page 437 or Windows-1252. Use the Unicode codepoint U+2297 in HTML, CSS or the Character Viewer instead.

How do I type ⊗ without a numpad?

Use the Windows Character Viewer (Win+.), the macOS Character Viewer (⌃⌘Space), an HTML entity such as ⊗, or copy the character directly from this page.

Why does Alt+8855 not work?

Alt+8855 only works on a keyboard with a physical numeric keypad. It also requires the application to accept the numeric-keypad input path. Laptops without a numpad need an alternative method.

What is the Unicode for Circled Times?

The Unicode codepoint for Circled Times is U+2297. You can use this value in HTML as ⊗, in CSS as \2297, and in Word with Alt+X.

How do I type ⊗ on a Mac?

Open the Character Viewer with ⌃⌘Space and search for the character name or U+2297, then click it.
